issue.title: test_handoff_end_to_end_settles_through_proc flakes under full just check, passes in isolation
issue.description:
## Flake report

- **Test:** `tests/tool/test_handoff.py::test_handoff_end_to_end_settles_through_proc`
- **Repro:** `just check` (4-worker full lane)

Proposed by sase-17d.12.2 note #3 during the agent-deck spread inspection. The node failed under a 4-worker full `just check` and passed in isolation on the same tree. The phase note does not record the exception text. Fail rate from that report: 1 full-lane failure, then a pass in isolation. The deck diff does not touch tool handoff. The land agent did not re-run the full lane.

payload.entry: Landing triage of proposed follow-up sase-1ou.2.1.2 note 2: complete handoff file passes21/21 on the fixed core, but this original report has no exception signature and no old-core failure was reproduced. Duplicate classification with sase-18t is unproven; leave open and decline duplicate closure or a second task. Audited evidence file:explicit:b0d1fd4be5d7f8c6c632927d. Outer lander sase-1ou.land retains closure judgment.

sase-1ou landing (2026-10-28): sase-18t closed done on the core store-contention fix. Duplicate closure of this bead is still declined: the original report has no exception signature, so attribution to the SQLite mechanism stays unproven. Whether this bead counts as a dormant flake is left to the next backlog re-triage.

Backlog triage (2026-11-27), verified on master 6b58ad0fe2: 4a7ce0f330 (2026-11-07) rewrote tests/tool/test_handoff.py::test_handoff_end_to_end_settles_through_proc. It drops the wall-clock 'assert elapsed < 2.0', proves non-waiting with a release file, and uses LOAD_TOLERANT_TIMEOUT for the proc waits. The other suspected mechanism (sase-18t SQLite store contention) was closed done on 10-28. 0 failures in the 30-day records.
